Calling it a 'pace car' is a little silly.

Why?

Because it's only the pace car exactly once (except in some REALLY rare cases). It's the pace car at the start of the race, when they do the formation lap.

After that, every time you see it, it's not the pace car. It is the 'safety car.' You see it far more often as a safety car than you do as a pace car. In most series, you see it every time there's a FCY. In some, it doesn't come out until it's FCY SC. (Full Course Yellow, usually shown with a combination of yellow flags being displayed in a specific manner and very frequently with a signboard that says "FCY" and an "SC" sign sometimes added with it, but I digress.)

Actually, seeing as I digressed that far, there's also a "virtual safety car." The race director tells everyone to slow down on the count of (usually) five or ten. They all must slow down to a specific speed (varies, plan on 50 to 80 kph) and maintain position. Because everyone slows down and then later speeds up at the same time, nobody is supposed to gain and advantage. If you're just watching NASCAR or even F1, you won't see things like that.

Now, if for some reason they restart the race AND the car appears again, then that time it was a pace car for a second time. That's exceedingly rare, but does sometimes happen.

So, the next time you're drinking and watching a race and your buddy says "pace car" after the formation lap, you can tell 'em that they're wrong and that it's really the safety car.
